findings.title: Cache is not re-checked after taking the write lock, so concurrent callers each reload the manifest
findings.body:
On a cold cache, several goroutines can see `ret == nil` under the read lock and then queue on `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`. After acquiring the write lock, none of them re-checks `entryPointAssetsCache`. Each one in turn re-reads and re-parses `assets-manifest.json` (or would hit the CDN), even after the first goroutine has already filled the cache.

This disk or network I/O runs while holding the exclusive lock. Every other request, including ones that would hit the cache, is serialized behind it.

Fix: after `Lock()`, add the usual double-check, `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`. Alternatively, use `sync.Once` or singleflight for the non-dev path.
